slot.brief: Count elements in exactly one of two/three overlapping sets using a Venn-diagram style inclusion-exclusion computation.

stem: Given $|A|=30$, $|B|=28$, $|C|=24$, $|A\cap B|=10$, $|A\cap C|=8$, $|B\cap C|=9$ and $|A\cap B\cap C|=4$, how many elements belong to exactly one set?

draft.stem: Given $|A|=30$, $|B|=28$, $|C|=24$, $|A\cap B|=10$, $|A\cap C|=8$, $|B\cap C|=9$ and $|A\cap B\cap C|=4$, how many elements belong to exactly one set?
draft.working:
Exactly one $=|A|+|B|+|C|-2\bigl(|A\cap B|+|A\cap C|+|B\cap C|\bigr)+3|A\cap B\cap C|$
$=30+28+24-2(10+8+9)+3(4)=40$.
draft.distractor_notes: A: omits the correction for the triple intersection. B: adds the triple intersection only once. D: uses the union formula instead of counting elements in exactly one set.
